literal: Sun Teng; Gao Longzhi; Sima Ziru
idiomatic: Sun Teng; Gao Longzhi; Sima Ziru

literal: Sun Teng, styled Longque, was a native of Shi'an in Xianyang.
idiomatic: Sun Teng, styled Longque, was a native of Shi'an in Xianyang.

literal: His grandfather Tong served the Juqu clan as Attendant Drafting at the Central Secretariat; when the Juqu were destroyed he entered Wei and settled on the northern frontier.
idiomatic: His grandfather Tong served the Juqu clan as attendant drafting at the central secretariat; when the Juqu were destroyed he entered Wei and settled on the northern frontier.

literal: When Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted Tong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke over the Masses, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yong Province; Teng's father Ji was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: When Sun Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his grandfather Tong bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, grand general of agile cavalry, duke over the masses, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Yong Province; his father Ji received bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province.

literal: Teng from youth was honest and straightforward, and clearly understood administrative affairs.
idiomatic: From youth Sun Teng was honest and straightforward, with a clear grasp of administrative affairs.

literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when the north was in turmoil, Teng threaded through danger and peril and reached Xiurong.
idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when the north was in turmoil, Sun Teng threaded through danger and peril and reached Xiurong.

literal: When Erzhu Rong raised righteousness, Teng followed Rong into Luoyang and by precedent was made Supernumerary Vice Master of Attendants.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong raised righteousness, Sun Teng followed him into Luoyang and by precedent was made supernumerary vice master of attendants.

literal: Soon he became chief clerk of the Grand Ancestor's headquarters and followed the Grand Ancestor east to campaign against Xing Gao.
idiomatic: Soon he became chief clerk of Gao Huan's headquarters and followed Gao Huan east to campaign against Xing Gao.

literal: When the army halted at Qi city, soldiers of the Fu Yi garrison plotted rebellion and were about to kill the commander.
idiomatic: When the army halted at Qi city, soldiers of the Fu Yi garrison plotted rebellion and were about to kill the commander.

literal: Teng learned of it and secretly reported to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Sun Teng learned of it and secretly reported to Gao Huan.

literal: Before long the affair broke out; because the Grand Ancestor was prepared, he captured and crushed them.
idiomatic: Before long the affair broke out; because Gao Huan was prepared, he captured and crushed them.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor became governor of Jin Province, Teng served as chief clerk, was additionally made Rear General, and was enfeoffed Baron of Shi'an County.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan became governor of Jin Province, Sun Teng served as chief clerk, was additionally made rear general, and was enfeoffed baron of Shi'an County.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor left Jinyang by Fukou and marched to Xiangyuan, Erzhu Zhao led troops in pursuit.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan left Jinyang by Fukou and marched to Xiangyuan, Erzhu Zhao led troops in pursuit.

literal: The Grand Ancestor and Zhao feasted and drank at the water's edge, swore brotherhood, and each returned to his own camp.
idiomatic: Gao Huan and Zhao feasted and drank at the water's edge, swore brotherhood, and each returned to his own camp.

literal: Next day Zhao again summoned the Grand Ancestor; the Grand Ancestor wished to reassure him and was about to go, but as he was mounting his horse Teng seized his robe and stopped him.
idiomatic: Next day Zhao summoned Gao Huan again; Gao Huan wished to reassure him and was about to ride to him, but as he was mounting his horse Sun Teng seized his robe and held him back.

literal: Zhao then railed wantonly across the water and galloped back to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Zhao cursed him from across the river and galloped back to Jinyang.

literal: The Grand Ancestor thereupon marched east.
idiomatic: Gao Huan thereupon marched east.

literal: When he raised righteousness at Xindu, Teng for his loyalty and sincerity was constantly included in planning.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised righteousness at Xindu, Sun Teng for his loyalty and sincerity was constantly included in planning.

literal: Teng held that with the court cut off and isolated, commands had nowhere to attach; if they did not provisionally establish someone, the multitude would lose heart and scatter — he urgently pleaded with the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Sun Teng argued that with the court cut off, commands had nowhere to attach; if they did not provisionally establish a ruler, the army would lose heart and scatter — he urgently pleaded with Gao Huan.

literal: The Grand Ancestor followed his counsel and thereupon established the restoration sovereign.
idiomatic: Gao Huan followed his counsel and thereupon established the restoration sovereign.

literal: Teng was made Palace Attendant, and soon additionally Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander of Displaced Populations in Six Provinces, and Grand Chief of the Northern Circuit.
idiomatic: Sun Teng was made palace attendant, and soon additionally bearer of the staff of authority, grand commander of displaced populations in six provinces, and grand chief of the northern circuit.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor marched on Ye, at first he left Duan Rong to hold Xindu; soon he sent Rong to garrison Zhongshan and still had Teng remain to guard the city.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched on Ye, at first he left Duan Rong to hold Xindu; soon he sent Rong to garrison Zhongshan and still had Sun Teng remain to guard the city.

literal: When Ye was pacified, Teng was appointed Governor of Xiang Province, his title was changed to Duke of Xianyang Commandery, his fief was increased to one thousand three hundred households in all, and he entered court as Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: When Ye was pacified, Sun Teng was appointed governor of Xiang Province, his title was changed to duke of Xianyang Commandery with a fief increased to one thousand three hundred households in all, and he entered court as palace attendant.

literal: At that time the daughter of Prince Yu of Jingzhao, Princess Pingyuan, was widowed and living alone; Teng wished to marry her, but the princess refused.
idiomatic: At that time the daughter of Prince Yu of Jingzhao, Princess Pingyuan, was widowed and living alone; Sun Teng wished to marry her, but the princess refused.

literal: Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi had no wife, and the princess wished to marry him; Teng, jealous of Longzhi, then sowed discord between them.
idiomatic: Palace attendant Feng Longzhi had no wife, and the princess wished to marry him; Sun Teng, jealous of Longzhi, then sowed discord between them.

literal: The Grand Ancestor memorialized to dismiss Teng from office and requested that he be sent out on external appointment; before long he was restored.
idiomatic: Gao Huan memorialized to dismiss Sun Teng from office and requested that he be sent out on external appointment; before long he was restored.

literal: Because Teng was the Grand Ancestor's trusted confidant, he entered and dwelt in the Secretariat, and together with Husi Chun managed confidential affairs.
idiomatic: Because Sun Teng was Gao Huan's trusted confidant, he entered and dwelt in the secretariat, and together with Husi Chun managed confidential affairs.

literal: Chun then harbored divergent designs and went astray at every turn.
idiomatic: Chun then harbored divergent designs and went astray at every turn.

literal: Teng saw deeply that he was suspected, feared disaster would reach him, and secretly led more than ten horsemen in a dash to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Sun Teng saw that he was deeply suspected, feared disaster would reach him, and secretly led more than ten horsemen in a dash to Jinyang.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor entered to punish Husi Chun, he left Teng to administer Bing Province affairs; he also had Teng serve as Vice Master of the Mobile Office for the eight provinces of Ji, Xiang, Yin, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, and An, administering Ji Province affairs, and again administering Xiang Province affairs.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered to punish Husi Chun, he left Sun Teng to administer Bing Province affairs; he also had Teng serve as vice master of the mobile office for the eight provinces of Ji, Xiang, Yin, Ding, Cang, Ying, You, and An, administering Ji Province affairs, and again administering Xiang Province affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Teng entered court as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; in internal and external affairs Teng knew all, and concurrently held Minister of Works and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, Sun Teng entered court as left vice director of the masters of writing; in internal and external affairs he knew all, and concurrently held minister of works and director of the masters of writing.

literal: At that time Western Wei sent generals to raid Southern Yan Province; an edict made Teng Grand Chief of the Southern Circuit and ordered him to lead the generals in suppressing them.
idiomatic: At that time Western Wei sent generals to raid Southern Yan Province; an edict made Sun Teng grand chief of the southern circuit and ordered him to lead the generals in suppressing them.

literal: Teng by nature was feeble and timid, without martial prestige or strategy; he lost the battle and returned.
idiomatic: Sun Teng by nature was feeble and timid, without martial prestige or strategy; he lost the battle and returned.

literal: He was again made Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: He was again made minister over the masses.

literal: At first, when the northern frontier was in turmoil, he lost a daughter; when he rose high he searched for her far and wide but never found her, and suspected she had become someone's slave.
idiomatic: At first, when the northern frontier was in turmoil, he lost a daughter; when he rose high he searched for her far and wide but never found her, and suspected she had become someone's slave.

literal: When he became Minister over the Masses, slaves and maidservants claiming to be free persons — without investigating truth or falsehood — were in every case freed; he hoped to free a thousand persons and thereby recover his daughter.
idiomatic: When he became minister over the masses, slaves and maidservants claiming to be free persons — without investigating truth or falsehood — were in every case freed; he hoped to free a thousand persons and thereby recover his daughter.

literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor entered court, and those around him spoke of it; the Grand Ancestor was greatly angered and removed him from the ministry.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan entered court, and those around him spoke of it; Gao Huan was greatly angered and removed him from the ministry.

literal: In the Wuding era he was sent to Qing Province to register floating and absentee households, and was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was sent to Qing Province to register floating and absentee households, and was transferred to grand preceptor.

literal: At first, Cui Xiaofen of Boling took a poor family's daughter of the Jia clan as a foster daughter; when Xiaofen died, his wife Yuan remarried Zheng Boyou and took Jia with her to the Zheng household.
idiomatic: At first, Cui Xiaofen of Boling took a poor family's daughter of the Jia clan as a foster daughter; when Xiaofen died, his wife Yuan remarried Zheng Boyou and took Jia with her to the Zheng household.

literal: Jia was beautiful in appearance; Teng took her in and at first made her a concubine.
idiomatic: Jia was beautiful in appearance; Sun Teng took her in and at first made her a concubine.

literal: When his wife Lady Yuan died, Teng because Jia had borne a son formally made her his wife; an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Danyang Commandery, and he again requested that Lady Yuan's title be transferred to her daughter.
idiomatic: When his wife Lady Yuan died, Sun Teng because Jia had borne a son formally made her his wife; an edict enfeoffed her as lady of Danyang Commandery, and he again requested that Lady Yuan's title be transferred to her daughter.

literal: Disregarding ritual and indulging desire — there were many cases of this kind.
idiomatic: Disregarding ritual and indulging desire — there were many cases of this kind.

literal: Teng early attached himself to the Grand Ancestor; through hardship and danger he labored diligently with respectful care and was deeply trusted and favored.
idiomatic: Sun Teng early attached himself to Gao Huan; through hardship and danger he labored diligently with respectful care and was deeply trusted and favored.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor placed him in the Wei court and entrusted him as a confidant, his spirit grew proud and overbearing; granting and taking were at his own will, and he sought bribes beyond reckoning.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan placed him in the Wei court and entrusted him as a confidant, his spirit grew proud and overbearing; granting and taking were at his own will, and he sought bribes beyond reckoning.

literal: Offices in life, posthumous gifts in death — none were granted without payment; stored silver vessels from tribute feasts he stole as household goods; he consorted closely with petty men and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth.
idiomatic: Offices in life, posthumous gifts in death — none were granted without payment; stored silver vessels from tribute feasts he stole as household goods; he consorted closely with petty men and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth.

literal: At Ye, together with Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru he was called one of the Four Dignitaries; lawless and willful, they did as they pleased — Teng was the worst of them.
idiomatic: At Ye, together with Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru he was called one of the Four Dignitaries; lawless and willful, they did as they pleased — Sun Teng was the worst of them.

literal: The Grand Ancestor repeatedly censured and reproved him, but in the end he would not repent and reform; court and countryside deeply scorned and mocked him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan repeatedly censured and reproved him, but in the end he would not repent and reform; court and countryside deeply scorned and mocked him.

literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Wuding he died, aged sixty-eight.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year of Wuding he died, aged sixty-eight.

literal: Posthumously he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, and the rest, Governor of Ji Province, Grand Preceptor, Opener of a Government Office, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Wen.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, and the rest, governor of Ji Province, grand preceptor, opener of a government office, and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing; his posthumous title was Wen.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, because Teng had aided in establishing the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, because Sun Teng had aided in establishing the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifice announced at his tomb.

literal: In the Huangjian era he was given associated sacrifice in the Grand Ancestor's temple court.
idiomatic: In the Huangjian era he was given associated sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.

literal: His son Fengzhen succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Fengzhen succeeded.

literal: Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: Gao Longzhi, styled Yanxing, was originally surnamed Xu and claimed descent from Jinxiang in Gaoping.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi, styled Yanxing, was originally surnamed Xu and claimed descent from Jinxiang in Gaoping.

literal: His father Gan served as Administrator of Baishui Commandery in Wei; he was adopted by his aunt's husband the Gao clan and therefore took their surname.
idiomatic: His father Gan served as administrator of Baishui Commandery in Wei; he was adopted by his aunt's husband the Gao clan and therefore took their surname.

literal: When Longzhi rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted Gan Duke over the Masses and Governor of Yong Province.
idiomatic: When Gao Longzhi rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his father Gan duke over the masses and governor of Yong Province.

literal: Because Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, the Grand Ancestor ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Liaoren in Bohai.
idiomatic: Because Gao Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, Gao Huan ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Liaoren in Bohai.

literal: Longzhi stood eight feet in height, with a fine beard and whiskers, and was deep and reserved in spirit with strong ambition.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi stood eight feet in height, with a fine beard and whiskers, and was deep and reserved in spirit with strong ambition.

literal: When Prince Yue of Runan was Governor of Si Province, Longzhi was made a clerk in the household bureau.
idiomatic: When Prince Yue of Runan was governor of Si Province, Gao Longzhi was made a clerk in the household bureau.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he first received office as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; with the mobile office of Yu Hui he went out to suppress Yang Kan at Mount Tai; Hui brought Longzhi in as a mobile office director, and Longzhi was additionally made Gentlemen Attendant.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, he first received office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; with the mobile office of Yu Hui he went out to suppress Yang Kan at Mount Tai; Hui brought Longzhi in as a mobile office director, and Longzhi was additionally made gentlemen attendant.

literal: He and the Grand Ancestor formed a deep personal bond.
idiomatic: He and Gao Huan formed a deep personal bond.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor came to Jin Province, Longzhi was brought in as administrator and administered Pingyang Commandery affairs.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan came to Jin Province, Gao Longzhi was brought in as administrator and administered Pingyang Commandery affairs.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness in Shandong and was made right deputy of the mobile office.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness in Shandong and was made right deputy of the mobile office.

literal: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, he was made Imperial Censor and concurrently Chief of the Imperial Kitchen.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wei Zhongxing, he was made imperial censor and concurrently chief of the imperial kitchen.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Ye and administered Xiang Province affairs.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in pacifying Ye and administered Xiang Province affairs.

literal: He followed in the defeat of the four Erzhu at Hanling; at the beginning of Taichang he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Opener of a Government Office Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: He followed in the defeat of the four Erzhu at Hanling; at the beginning of Taichang he was made grand general of agile cavalry and opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Longzhi over wine; the emperor was made to sit and was dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Gao Longzhi over wine; the emperor was made to sit and was dismissed from office.

literal: The Grand Ancestor blamed Longzhi for failing to keep harmony and memorialized to send him out as Grand Chief of the Northern Circuit; he was transferred to Governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.
idiomatic: Gao Huan blamed Gao Longzhi for failing to keep harmony and memorialized to send him out as grand chief of the northern circuit; he was transferred to governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed duke of Pingyuan Commandery with a fief of one thousand seven hundred households.

literal: Longzhi requested a reduction of seven hundred households in his fief and also asked to lower his own rank by four steps in favor of his elder brother Teng; both were granted by special edict, and Teng was still made Governor of Cang Province.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi requested a reduction of seven hundred households in his fief and also asked to lower his own rank by four steps in favor of his elder brother Sun Teng; both were granted by special edict, and Sun Teng was still made governor of Cang Province.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor punished Husi Chun, Longzhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing of the Grand Mobile Office.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan punished Husi Chun, Gao Longzhi was made director of the masters of writing of the grand mobile office.

literal: When the Grand Marshal, Prince Chang of Qinghe, assumed provisional authority, Longzhi was appointed Palace Attendant, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently Imperial Censor.
idiomatic: When the grand marshal, Prince Chang of Qinghe, assumed provisional authority, Gao Longzhi was appointed palace attendant, right vice director of the masters of writing, and concurrently imperial censor.

literal: He spent lavishly on labor and greatly built temples and pagodas, and was reproved by the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: He spent lavishly on labor and greatly built temples and pagodas, and was reproved by Gao Huan.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict recalled him as Governor of Bing Province, and he entered court as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict recalled him as governor of Bing Province, and he entered court as right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: At that time land was first being allotted to commoners; the powerful and noble all seized the good and fertile, while the poor and weak all received the thin and poor.
idiomatic: At that time land was first being allotted to commoners; the powerful and noble all seized the good and fertile, while the poor and weak all received the thin and poor.

literal: Longzhi reported to the Grand Ancestor, and all were reversed and exchanged, and thus fairness was achieved.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi reported to Gao Huan, and all were reversed and exchanged, and thus fairness was achieved.

literal: He also concurrently served as Grand General of Construction and oversaw all building in the capital.
idiomatic: He also concurrently served as grand general of construction and oversaw all building in the capital.

literal: He expanded and built the southern city, twenty-five li in circuit.
idiomatic: He expanded and built the southern city, twenty-five li in circuit.

literal: Because the Zhang River lay close to the imperial city, he raised a long dike to guard against flooding.
idiomatic: Because the Zhang River lay close to the imperial city, he raised a long dike to guard against flooding.

literal: He also dug canals to draw the Zhang River in circuit around the city walls, built water-powered mills, and all were of benefit to the age.
idiomatic: He also dug canals to draw the Zhang River in circuit around the city walls, built water-powered mills, and all were of benefit to the age.

literal: From Xiaochang onward in Wei, the realm was much troubled; governors and prefects all served as commanders of their districts, and though there were no military affairs they all established assistant staffs — everywhere this became quite troublesome.
idiomatic: From Xiaochang onward in Wei, the realm was much troubled; governors and prefects all served as commanders of their districts, and though there were no military affairs they all established assistant staffs — everywhere this became quite troublesome.

literal: Longzhi submitted a memorial requesting that unless they were truly on the frontier and actually had troops and horses, all such appointments be cut off.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi submitted a memorial requesting that unless they were truly on the frontier and actually had troops and horses, all such appointments be cut off.

literal: Also many court nobles falsely held the rank of regular attendant to obtain the insignia of the diao and chan; Longzhi himself submitted a memorial resigning his palace attendant rank and also listed those who held false attendant rank and their regalia, requesting that they too be abolished.
idiomatic: Also many court nobles falsely held the rank of regular attendant to obtain the insignia of the diao and chan; Gao Longzhi himself submitted a memorial resigning his palace attendant rank and also listed those who held false attendant rank and their regalia, requesting that they too be abolished.

literal: An edict approved all as he had memorialized.
idiomatic: An edict approved all as he had memorialized.

literal: Because military and state affairs were many, those who falsely claimed names and stole offices were beyond counting; Longzhi submitted a request for inspection and registration, obtaining more than fifty thousand persons, but the petty men raised an uproar and Longzhi, in fear, stopped.
idiomatic: Because military and state affairs were many, those who falsely claimed names and stole offices were beyond counting; Gao Longzhi submitted a request for inspection and registration, obtaining more than fifty thousand persons, but the petty men raised an uproar and Longzhi, in fear, stopped.

literal: An edict ordered him to supervise affairs of imperial record and advanced his rank to Duke over the Masses.
idiomatic: An edict ordered him to supervise affairs of imperial record and advanced his rank to duke over the masses.

literal: In the Wuding era he served as commissioner for registering households in Hebei.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he served as commissioner for registering households in Hebei.

literal: Recalled, he was appointed General of the Palace Guard and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and soon additionally Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Recalled, he was appointed general of the palace guard and recorder of the affairs of the masters of writing, and soon additionally palace attendant.

literal: He again went out to administer Qing Province affairs.
idiomatic: He again went out to administer Qing Province affairs.

literal: Recalled, he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and transferred to Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: Recalled, he was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent, concurrently left vice director of the masters of writing and director of the ministry of personnel, and transferred to grand preceptor.

literal: At that time Shizong was administering affairs; customs were stern and pure, but Longzhi at times accepted bribes; Shizong greatly reproached and humiliated him at the Masters of Writing office.
idiomatic: At that time Gao Cheng was administering affairs; customs were stern and pure, but Gao Longzhi at times accepted bribes; Gao Cheng greatly reproached and humiliated him at the masters of writing office.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, Longzhi's rank was advanced to prince.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Gao Longzhi's rank was advanced to prince.

literal: Soon, retaining his former office, he recorded the affairs of the Masters of Writing, served as Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and supervised the national history.
idiomatic: Soon, retaining his former office, he recorded the affairs of the masters of writing, served as grand director of the imperial clan, and supervised the national history.

literal: Longzhi by nature was fussy over small things; as for the state's ceremonial regalia, the hundred entertainments, and dress regulations, he at times made changes and did not follow ancient precedent — contemporary opinion criticized this.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi by nature was fussy over small things; as for the state's ceremonial regalia, the hundred entertainments, and dress regulations, he at times made changes and did not follow ancient precedent — contemporary opinion criticized this.

literal: At the shooting butts he set up three human figures in a posture of martial valor.
idiomatic: At the shooting butts he set up three human figures in a posture of martial valor.

literal: Xianzu once came to the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Longzhi, "At the shooting butts one could make fierce beasts to preserve the ancient meaning — why set up human figures?
idiomatic: Gao Yang once came to the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Gao Longzhi, "At the shooting butts one could make fierce beasts to preserve the ancient meaning — why set up human figures?

literal: Shooting at human figures all day — that I will not accept.
idiomatic: Shooting at human figures all day — that I will not accept.

literal: " Longzhi had nothing to reply.
idiomatic: " Gao Longzhi had nothing to reply.

literal: At first, Shizong entrusted affairs to Right Vice Director Cui Xian, Gentlemen Attendant Cui Jishu, and others; when Shizong died, Longzhi reported to Xianzu that they should all be killed, but permission was not granted.
idiomatic: At first, Gao Cheng entrusted affairs to right vice director Cui Xian, gentlemen attendant Cui Jishu, and others; when Gao Cheng died, Gao Longzhi reported to Gao Yang that they should all be killed, but permission was not granted.

literal: Xianzu because Longzhi was an elder in years entrusted him with government affairs; Jishu and the others still because of old grievances slandered him, saying, "Whenever Longzhi sees those who come to sue, he always adds a note of pity to show that he himself cannot judge the case.
idiomatic: Gao Yang because Gao Longzhi was an elder in years entrusted him with government affairs; Jishu and the others still because of old grievances slandered him, saying, "Whenever Longzhi sees those who come to sue, he always adds a note of pity to show that he himself cannot judge the case.

literal: Since Xianzu's commission to him was heavy, when he knew there were unjust cases he should readily have cleared them — how could he shift blame to win a name? This was not the conduct of a great minister.
idiomatic: Since Gao Yang's commission to him was heavy, when he knew there were unjust cases he should readily have cleared them — how could he shift blame to win renown? This was not the conduct of a great minister.
